default.notes: Not eligible for the eVisa or visa on arrival — a visit visa must be arranged before travel through a sponsor in Bahrain (a hotel, company or relative) via the Nationality, Passport & Residence Affairs (NPRA).

groups.notes: GCC citizens may enter Bahrain freely under Gulf Cooperation Council arrangements — a national ID card is accepted and no visa is needed.

Eligible for a visa on arrival (about BHD 5 for a 2-week stay, extendable) at Bahrain International Airport and the King Fahd Causeway, or apply online in advance for an eVisa on evisa.gov.bh — longer and multi-entry options are offered online.

Eligible to apply online for a Bahrain eVisa on evisa.gov.bh before travel — accommodation details and a return ticket are required, and eligibility can be conditional (for some nationalities on residence or prior visas), so check the portal and obtain the eVisa before flying rather than relying on a visa on arrival.

BH.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Bahraini citizens.

IL.notes: Following the 2020 normalisation agreement Israeli passport holders have been able to obtain Bahraini visas, but arrangements remain sensitive to regional events and practical access has fluctuated — verify the current position on evisa.gov.bh or with a Bahraini mission before booking.

IR.notes: Relations between Bahrain and Iran are strained — a sponsored visa is required and approval is discretionary; confirm with a Bahraini mission before making plans.
